coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: 13 days out, you run the long run today. Your recovery score is 89/100 and RHR dropped to 56—you're fresh. Build to 14–16 miles with 1,200–1,500 ft of vert, done entirely at Z2 (140–150 bpm based on recent data). This is your final chance to feel the alpine terrain under your legs without fatigue debt. Keep it steady, not fast. Practice your fueling rhythm: aim for 200–250 cal/hour via whatever you'll use in Slovenia. The goal is confidence and palatability, not effort.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You slept 8 hours with 93.9% efficiency—that's elite prep. Eat a familiar breakfast 90 min before you leave: 60g carb + 15g protein (bagel + peanut butter, oatmeal + egg, etc.). On the run, hit 50–60g carbs/hour via gels, chews, or real food—whatever you've tested. Post-run within 30 min: 40g carb + 20g protein to arrest glycogen depletion and begin adaptation. You've run 35.6 miles this week; you're in a taper, so don't underfuel thinking "less work = less hunger." You need the fuel to recover.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your sleep profile is locked in. Tonight, aim for 8+ hours again—non-negotiable. Post-run, foam roll your feet, calves, and IT band for 8 min; ice bath is optional but 10–12 min at 50°F will blunt inflammation if you've got soreness. Elevate legs for 20 min while eating. Your 30-day avg RHR was 65.4, now 56: you're adapted and recovered. Don't overthink it. If you feel sore tomorrow (Sunday), take it easy—you're 11 days from race day and any niggle compounds fast.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: This is your last long run. Use it to visualize the descent from Kranjska Gora's north face—steep, technical, loose. Practice foot placement and rhythm so your brain has a template on race day. The Julian Alps demand precision on the downhill; your aerobic engine is ready, but your CNS needs the script. Run strong but controlled. After this week, your volume drops 30–40% and intensity stays light—that psychological shift from work to rest is real. Embrace it. You've earned the confidence to taper.
